## Summary

The IEEE registry lists 1,235 MA-L blocks to "Cisco Systems, Inc", mostly at West Tasman Drive in San Jose, California, and one to "Cisco Systems Inc" at the Stella Building in Swindon, UK [1]. Cisco was founded in December 1984 by Leonard Bosack and Sandy Lerner, is headquartered in San Jose, trades on Nasdaq as CSCO, and makes routers, network switches, firewalls and security software, UCS servers, Webex and IP phones; it bought Linksys in 2003 and sold it to Belkin in 2013 [2]. The registry's separate "Cisco Meraki", "Cisco SPVTG" and "Cisco-Linksys, LLC" names are not aliases of this entry [1].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely enterprise network gear: a router, switch, access point or IP phone [1][2][3]. The Catalyst 9136 Series is a Wi-Fi 6E 802.11ax access point with 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz radios and an integrated Bluetooth Low Energy 5 radio for location use cases; Cisco's datasheet names no chipset [3]. Cisco's FCC grantee codes are listed as LDK, UDX and PKW [4]. CVE-2023-20198, published in October 2023, covers the observed exploitation of the web UI feature of Cisco IOS XE Software for initial access [5].

Silicon and randomization are not documented by the sources consulted; the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session, so no filing under these codes was checked.
